Here is a number every executive should internalize: 42%.

That is the percentage of enterprise AI cases where Stanford researchers found the AI model itself was wholly interchangeable. Across 51 deployments in seven countries, nine industries, and 14 business functions, the technology was rarely the differentiator.

The real barriers? Process redesign. Trust across teams. Organizational understanding. Data infrastructure. The human and structural work that does not make headlines but determines whether AI creates value or stays stuck in pilot mode.

This is critical context as the flagship model race accelerates. GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Ultra — all capable, all improving rapidly. But if your organization cannot execute around whatever model you choose, swapping to the latest release changes nothing.

The companies succeeding with AI are treating it as an operating model transformation, not a technology purchase. They are investing in readiness, not just capability.
